description_full: Diodes Incorporated, together with its subsidiaries, provides semiconductor products in Asia, the Americas, and Europe. The company offers MOSFET and SiC MOSFET discrete semiconductor products; data line protection, power line protection, thyrister, USB Type-C protection, and transient voltage suppressor protection devices; Schottky diodes, small signal switching diodes, Zener diodes, and SiC diodes; and bridges, super barrier rectifiers, Schottky rectifiers, Schottky bridge rectifiers, and fast and ultra-fast rectifiers. It also provides avalanche transistors, gate driver transistors, and pre-bias transistors; power management devices, such as AC-DC and DC-DC converters, digital isolators and isolated gate drivers, USB power switches, low dropout, photocoupler, and linear voltage regulators; standard linear devices, such as operational amplifiers and comparators, current monitors, voltage references, and reset generators; LED lighting drivers; audio amplifiers; and sensor products, including Hall-effect sensors and motor drivers. In addition, the company offers mixed-signal products comprising high speed mux/demux, digital switches, interface, redrivers, universal level shifters/voltage translators, clock ICs, and packet switches; low-voltage complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) and CMOS devices, as well as ultra-low power CMOS logic and analog switches; and multichip products, co-packaged discrete, analog, and mixed-signal silicon in miniature packages. Further, it provides silicon and silicon epitaxial wafers; frequency control products; and contact image sensors. The company serves industrial, automotive, computing, consumer, and communications end-markets through direct sales, marketing personnel, independent sales representatives, and distributors. Diodes Incorporated was incorporated in 1959 and is headquartered in Plano, Texas.

financial_summary: Diodes Incorporated is a mid-cap technology business with a $4.0B market cap on $1.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -10% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 15% against a 11% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 34%.

The business throws off $137M in free cash flow — roughly 9 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.26× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 13× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 0.8%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 2.6% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 2% operating margin is roughly in line with the Technology median (7%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.10x its revenue share).
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-34.4% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 102% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 6% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 31% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 70% and a beta of 1.39, it amplifies market moves, though its beta has shifted (1y 2.42 vs 5y 1.62), so read it loosely.
About $45.1M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 44% in the 2020 crash, 46% in the 2022 bear market and 89% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $79.22 (margin of safety -10%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 60%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $50.10 to $131 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 34.9 vs 27.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 578% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 3.4% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 0.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 4 covering analysts target $127 on average, 45% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 15% earns above the cost of capital of 11.3%, but the 4pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.80).
It runs a 34% gross margin and converts 9% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 3.26x.
ROE of 4% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.3x equity multiplier).
It spends 10.9% of revenue on R&D and 1.7% on stock compensation.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $351.4M (9% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 5.8, in the safe zone).
Working capital ties up about 191 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -9.5% over 3 years, 3.8% over 5 years and 5.7% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 16%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 4.2% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex runs only 0.6x depreciation (5.3% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 11, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 20.6% on average.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.6%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (14 sales, net $4.8M sold).
Shareholder yield is a modest 0.8% (0.8% in buybacks).
people: With about 7,989 employees, each generates about $186K of revenue, 0.5x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 6.1% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $17K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.6M (9x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
